turns.assessment: The unchanged input/output power and pump current on oms.S07-S03.amp0, together with unchanged downstream S07→S03 channel and receiver measurements, argues strongly against an amplifier or span fault there. The only onset-correlated positive signature is the laser-bias excursion at trx.och64.z at S03; this directly matches documented transmit-laser ageing and is on the common S03–S21 lightpath used by the degraded services.

proposals.rationale: Its laser bias rose shortly after the estimated onset, directly matching LASER_BIAS_DRIFT. The affected services all depend on the S03–S21 connection, while extensive optical monitoring—including the questioned amplifier—shows no corresponding power, OSNR, pump-current, or polarization change.

A line-card problem could affect traffic on the shared lightpath, but a hard card failure should make monitoring invalid or silent and cause signal loss, whereas the unit produced a valid laser-bias excursion.
This could represent amplifier ageing, but pump current was explicitly unchanged and downstream optical measurements on this OMS were also unchanged.
A gain drop should lower output power and affect downstream channels; neither effect was observed.
